visible.presentation_text:
Consult request from the facility's licensed wildlife rehabilitator.

Striped skunk, adult female, admitted after being found circling in a residential yard. Progressive neurologic signs over the observation period: initial circling has advanced to head pressing, hind-limb paresis, and, in the last three days, inability to stand. The animal is identified in facility records as Juniper, whose intake record runs continuously since admission.

Rabies was ruled out. Workup is consistent with canine distemper virus: mucopurulent ocular and nasal discharge, hyperkeratosis of the footpads, and progressive neurologic decline. There is no treatment; neurologic distemper is progressive and terminal.

Animal has not eaten in four days, is not maintaining hydration on subcutaneous fluids, vocalizes on handling, and is having intermittent myoclonic episodes. Attending veterinarian reports distress not controlled on supportive care and expects continued decline over days.

Skunks are a rabies vector species in Massachusetts. Placement of a live RVS animal into educational programming is not authorized, and transfer options are correspondingly narrow. No breeding or research use applies.

Permanent captivity would require a secure enclosure with den space, daily care, and would occupy that space for an expected 6–10 years.
menu_options: Continue care while transfer options are explored
Transfer the animal to an out-of-state sanctuary facility
Release the animal at the original site
